Hi Laura,

Thanks for the continued work here. We're close on the DPA but need explicit confirmation on a couple of details before procurement will release the PO:

- Role/definitions: Acme needs Redwood to confirm the role (Controller vs Processor) specifically for embeddings generation — we treat generated embeddings as customer data.
- Logs & telemetry: we need clarity on retention of request logs and KV/embedding caches for audit purposes.
- Subprocessors: please confirm the current subprocessor list and the notification window for new subprocessors (Procurement prefers 30 days).
- Execution: procurement prefers DocuSign for signature, please share envelope.

Can you send a clean (executive) version and the working redline so our legal team can do a final pass? We can aim to sign this week if the items above are clarified.

Regards,
Jordan

Acme Analytics

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a redline (DPA_Redline_v3.pdf) and a short executive summary below. I copied Rishi and Monica so legal and sales are aligned.

Executive summary (short):
- Role: Redwood proposes to remain the Processor for customer-provided data and the Controller only where we process telemetry/aggregated metrics for platform health. Embeddings generated from Acme inputs are treated as Customer Data (Processor processing on behalf of Controller).
- Logs: Standard request logs retained for 60 days by default; KV cache/embeddings not persisted beyond inference lifecycle unless customer opts into retention for evaluation.
- Subprocessors: full list attached (Subprocessors_2026Q3.csv). Redwood provides 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; urgent security-critical subprocessors may be onboarded with notification and an option to opt-out within 10 days under defined conditions.
- Execution: we'll send a DocuSign envelope after final sign-off on the embedded clauses (link to follow).

Next steps: Rishi — see inline comments in the redline for controller/processor language. Monica — can you confirm procurement details and PO timing? Jordan — if procurement wants a slightly longer log retention window we can negotiate that (see Rishi's note).

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T15:34:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA finalization + embeddings handling (Acme)

Laura / Monica —

I reviewed the redline and left focused comments. Key items to surface to Acme (short bullets for Jordan):

1) Controller vs Processor:
- We should accept processor status for customer input/embedding generation. For telemetry/aggregated metrics we remain controller of our own operational data; add explicit carve-out clarifying aggregated metrics are pseudonymized and cannot be re-linked to a customer request.

2) Embeddings as Personal Data:
- If Acme feeds PII into prompts, embeddings could be considered personal data under certain regs. We will include a clause that treats embeddings as Customer Data and commits Redwood to delete or not persist embeddings unless Acme opts in and provides consent/controls. Add a short section: "Embeddings handling and optional retention" with clear opt-in.

3) Logs & Retention:
- Proposed compromise: default request logs 60 days; extended retention up to 180 days available under SOC2+ audit arrangement or explicit PO/addendum. KV cache and ephemeral caches are not durable by default.

4) Subprocessors:
- Provide current list (attached). For any new subprocessor, standard 30-day notice; include an express right to object and move to escalation flow (SLA credits not required but cooperation for remediation).

5) Transfers & SCCs:
- For EU transfers include EU SCCs + UK Addendum where applicable; ensure a DocuSign clause and signature capture for Controller/Processor appendix.

6) Security telemetry vs operational metrics:
- Separate security logs (used for incident response) from product telemetry; security logs may be retained 90 days for incident investigation if needed. We should offer Acme the option to request longer forensic retention with a commensurate fee.

Attachments: DPA_Redline_v3.pdf (with inline comments), Subprocessors_2026Q3.csv

Happy to join a short call with Acme legal if they want to walk through redlines.

-Rishi
General Counsel (acting) — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmeanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: DPA finalization + embeddings handling (Acme)

Laura / Rishi —

Quick responses after internal review:
- Controller/Processor: Acme accepts Redwood as Processor for embeddings so long as the DPA language explicitly states embeddings are Customer Data and Redwood will not use them to improve public models. Add a clause that prohibits using customer embeddings for generalized model training without explicit consent.
- Logs: procurement asks if we can get 90 days on security logs (for audit) vs 60 default for request logs.
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice is acceptable. Please confirm whether any subprocessors are US-based cloud providers (we need that for our internal transfer log).

Procurement note: attached our PO (Acme-PO-789.pdf). We need DocuSign completion and a signed DPA before we release the PO. Can you send the DocuSign envelope to procurements@acmeanalytics.com and myself?

Jordan
